title: From Idols to KOICA: South Korea’s Disaster Support for Nepal
author: Titiksha Devrani
text:
The Korea Disaster Relief Team (KDRT) deployed to Rasuwa, Nepal, to carry out search and rescue and emergency relief operations. after the devastating flood of Aug. 26, 2026.
Credit: KOICA Nepal Office
Following the destructive August 26 floods in Nepal, Lee Know of the K-pop boy band Stray Kids donated 100 million won (about $72,600) through World Vision. After Lee Know’s donation, his bandmate Felix donated 50 million won (about $37,000) to the Korean Committee for UNICEF, specifically for Nepal flood relief, on his birthday. Stray Kids’ leader Bang Chan followed with a 200 million won (about $144,000) donation, giving half to the Korean Committee for UNICEF for Nepal flood relief and half to Seoul Rehabilitation Hospital. The gestures echo acts of support for Nepal by other Korean personalities in the past. For example, figure skater Kim Yuna and actor Lee Min-ho (a different celebrity from Lee Know, whose birth name is also Lee Min-ho) extended aid to Nepal after the devastating earthquake in 2015. [...]
